verses.sa: वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्तिदंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि । केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषुसंदृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः ॥
verses.tr: Your blazing, terrible mouths swallow them in haste. Some are seen caught between your teeth, with crushed heads.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has been staring at the cosmic form, and now he sees the warriors he knows rushing toward certain destruction. Listen for the physical detail of how they enter.

body.text: Your blazing, terrible mouths swallow them in haste. Some are seen caught between your teeth, with crushed heads. Here Arjuna sees the great warriors getting caught between teeth. The heads are crushed. The war ends not with swords, but with bodies being swallowed. The next verse says these warriors rush into the mouths like rivers flowing to the sea.

verses.sa: यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाःसमुद्रमेवाभिमुखाः द्रवन्ति । तथा तवामी नरलोकवीराविशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति ॥
verses.tr: As many streams of water rush naturally toward the sea, so these great warriors of the world enter your blazing mouths.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Listen to the image Arjuna uses to show the warriors' fate.

body.text: As many streams of water rush naturally toward the sea, so these great warriors of the world enter your blazing mouths. Rivers run to the sea without choosing, and Arjuna sees the great warriors entering Krishna's mouths the same way. As moths rush into a flame, so the people rush into your blazing mouths to their own destruction.

verses.sa: यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गाविशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः । तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोकास्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः ॥
verses.tr: As moths rush with great speed into a blazing fire to their destruction, so these people rush with great speed into your mouths to their destruction.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna sees a terrifying sight: entire armies rushing into Krishna's cosmic mouths. Listen for the single image that captures their doom.

body.text: As moths rush with great speed into a blazing fire to their destruction, so these people rush with great speed into your mouths to their destruction. Notice the word patangah, moths, and the word jvalanam, fire. Like moths that rush to a flame and die, these people rush into your mouths for their own destruction. Krishna's mouths are devouring these warriors while also licking up all the worlds with fierce radiance.

verses.sa: लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ताल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः । तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रंभासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो ॥
verses.tr: You lick up all the worlds from every side with your blazing mouths. Your fierce radiance fills the whole universe and burns it, O Vishnu.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna stands before the cosmic form, and his voice breaks as he describes what he sees. Listen to the word that makes the universe sound like food.

body.text: You lick up all the worlds from every side with your blazing mouths. Your fierce radiance fills the whole universe and burns it, O Vishnu. Arjuna calls the blazing mouths that devour everything from every side. The word he uses is lelihyase, you lick up, so the universe is not just being destroyed, it is being eaten like a meal. He asks who this fierce form is and begs to know the purpose of this vision.

verses.sa: आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपोनमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद । विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यंन हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम् ॥
verses.tr: Tell me who You are in this fierce form. Salutations to You, best of the radiant beings; be gracious. I wish to know You, the primal one, for I do not understand Your purpose.
verses.angle: Arjuna's two questions: who and why
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna stops resisting. He bows to the cosmic terror and asks two plain questions: who are you in this form, and why? Listen for the second one.

body.text: Tell me who You are in this fierce form. Salutations to You, best of the radiant beings; be gracious. I wish to know You, the primal one, for I do not understand Your purpose. Arjuna asks to know the primal source of this vision. He says he does not know your purpose, and in that admission he surrenders his last demand for control. Krishna answers by naming himself Time, the destroyer of worlds, and tells Arjuna that the enemy warriors will not survive.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचकालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धोलोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः । ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वेयेऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः ॥
verses.tr: The Blessed Lord says: I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds, here to end all beings. Even without you, the warriors standing in the opposing ranks will not survive.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has just trembled before the cosmic form and demanded to know who this fierce being is. Now Krishna answers from within that vision.

body.text: The Blessed Lord says: I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds, here to end all beings. Even without you, the warriors standing in the opposing ranks will not survive. Krishna names himself as Time, the great destroyer. He tells Arjuna that the warriors in the opposing ranks are already doomed, and will die even without Arjuna lifting a single weapon. Krishna commands Arjuna to rise, telling him the enemy is already slain and he is merely the instrument.

verses.sa: तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्वजित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् । मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेवनिमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, rise and win fame. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by me; become only the instrument, Arjuna.
verses.angle: Nimittam: the instrument who acts without claim
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has shown Arjuna the cosmic form, and now he turns the vision into action. Listen to how he redefines the battle as a mere formality.

body.text: Therefore, rise and win fame. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by me; become only the instrument, Arjuna. Listen to the word nimittam, instrument. Krishna tells Arjuna that the enemies are already slain by him, so Arjuna must become merely the instrument, with no claim over the act or the result. Krishna lists the great warriors already slain by him, urging Arjuna to stand firm and fight.

verses.sa: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं चकर्णं तथाऽन्यानपि योधवीरान् । मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठायुध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान् ॥
verses.tr: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and the other great warriors have already been slain by Me. Do not falter; fight, and you will surely conquer your enemies in battle.
verses.angle: Krishna names the slain warriors to push Arjuna to fight
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has just seen the whole universe in one form. Now Krishna names the very warriors he fears, and tells him what to do.

body.text: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and the other great warriors have already been slain by Me. Do not falter; fight, and you will surely conquer your enemies in battle. Krishna names four of Arjuna's greatest teachers and rivals, Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and Karna, and says they have already been slain by Him. He then commands Arjuna to stop trembling and simply be the instrument to finish them. Sanjaya hears Arjuna's choked voice as he folds his hands and bows to Krishna, terrified by what he has just seen.

verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्यकृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी । नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णंसगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य ॥
verses.tr: Sanjaya says: Hearing Krishna's words, Arjuna trembled, folded his hands, bowed again and again, and spoke to Krishna in a choked voice, filled with fear.
verses.angle: Arjuna, the crowned warrior, is helpless
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Arjuna, the great warrior, has just seen the cosmic form. Listen to how he folds his hands and trembles before Krishna.

body.text: Sanjaya says: Hearing Krishna's words, Arjuna trembled, folded his hands, bowed again and again, and spoke to Krishna in a choked voice, filled with fear. The crowned warrior, Arjuna, who should be fighting, is reduced to trembling, folding his hands, and bowing again and again, unable to stand before the cosmic form. Arjuna now speaks, and his words begin by praising the very chanting that terrifies him.
